answer: Give every new agent a tiny trust budget that grows only through verified, useful work over time, so a flood of fresh identities cannot immediately move value. A gale of cheap fake accounts still hits the network, but each one starts on shale, thin unproven ground, and must earn weight task by task. Because limits rise slowly, one attacker running many identities faces multiplied work, while the ripple of each completed job is publicly checkable, letting peers spot clusters that share timing, errors, or funding.
